chunks: Yunus narrated from Sinan ibn Tariq, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying:
It is befitting for the believer to fear Allah, Exalted and Glorified, with a fear as if he is overlooking the Fire, and to hope in Him with a hope as if he is from the inhabitants of Paradise.
Then he said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is according to the expectation of His servant; if he expects good, it will be good, and if he expects evil, it will be evil.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper balance of fear and hope for a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes the balanced spiritual state of the believer, combining intense fear (khawf) as if standing before Hellfire with hopeful expectation (raja') as if already among the people of Paradise. It concludes with the principle of divine responsiveness to the servant's expectation (zann), where good expectations yield good outcomes and evil expectations yield evil ones. In Shia scholarship, this reflects the concept of 'tawassul' through positive expectation of God's mercy, encouraging believers to align their inner state with divine promise.
